scenes.title: Reminder
scenes.caption: A reminder about your Council Tax.
scenes.say: A reminder notice has come from your council about Council Tax. Here's what it says, and what to do.

scenes.title: Missed one
scenes.caption: The November instalment was not paid.
scenes.say: The council's records show the November instalment of one hundred and forty eight pounds, due on the first, has not been paid.

moves.cue: one hundred and forty eight pounds

scenes.title: Pay now
scenes.caption: Pay £148.00 within 7 days of the notice.
scenes.say: What to do is simple. Pay the one hundred and forty eight pounds within seven days, and you can carry on paying in instalments.

scenes.title: If you don't
scenes.caption: The whole year's bill falls due at once.
scenes.say: Miss that, and you lose the instalments. The rest of the year, seven hundred and forty pounds, is due all at once.

scenes.title: Court costs
scenes.caption: Court action could add £85.00 in costs.
scenes.say: If it's still unpaid, the council may go to the magistrates' court, and eighty five pounds of costs get added.

scenes.title: How to pay
scenes.caption: Online, by phone, or at a Post Office.
scenes.say: You can pay online, by phone at any hour, or at a Post Office or PayPoint with the barcode on your bill.

scenes.title: Need help?
scenes.caption: Struggling? Contact the council straight away.
scenes.say: Already paid? Ignore it. Struggling? Contact the council at once. There may be help with the cost, and Citizens Advice is free. Check with the council.

faults: scene 2: the cross is on the council, which reads as the council being wrong, when it is the home that has not paid; the letter that was sent does not show in the pictures

scene 3: the banknote sent from home to council is not shown, and the tick lands on the council as if it were approved, not on the payment; the clock floats up over the middle with its own badge, so it reads as two clocks

scene 4: the pile of coins is stacked on the house beside the warning and stands for the £740, so the picture shows two amounts. The warning bubble sits over the house roof and the count has no clear link to the pile
scene 6: a letter stands for a Post Office, and a computer for paying online; the letter is not what a Post Office is, so it is the wrong thing. PayPoint is not shown

scene 7: the council is drawn as a woman, a person in a suit, when the council is an organisation; the 'You' person is drawn yellow with a tick before anything has been said, and the tick reads as approval
scene 7: the picture shows only help being offered; it does not show the 'already paid' or 'Citizens Advice' ideas
